energy_gpu_range.verdict: CONFIRMED: 7.05 pJ is 500 W at 43 % and 11.17 pJ is 700 W at 38 %; the range spans the power estimate as well as the utilisation, and version 13 prints neither the power range nor the equation

energy_read_dominated.verdict: CONFIRMED (arithmetic): the reads alone give 32.49x and 18.18x. PARTLY already in version 13: it states the read share, that a low energy per operation is worth nothing without the accuracy, and that no energy-to-target trajectory is shown, but not plainly that the printed ratio itself is a per-operation, read-dominated figure, not energy to a quality

energy_cost_boundary.tt_term: e_tt = reads_pwr * (adc_j_per_conversion + sram_add_j): one ADC conversion and one read-add-write of H per read weight
energy_cost_boundary.adc: an 8-bit SAR conversion; the range spans the published survey's energy-efficient designs to conservative ones [murmann_adc]
energy_cost_boundary.sram: one read-add-write of the 16-32 bit buffer H per read weight (ours; cf. [horowitz2014])
not_in_the_model: AGAD's leaky average p and reference p_ref (their arithmetic beyond one buffer add)
energy_cost_boundary.verdict: CONFIRMED (wording): both phrases are in version 13 and refer to different costs, but the text does not say which

clipping.verdict: CONFIRMED: the losses are as quoted and the text calls clipping a policy, but proposes no pulse-length or update-management comparison

controls.verdict: CONFIRMED: version 13 says the ideal-device row is not an algorithm-only reference, but gives no control ladder

sgd_rate.verdict: CONFIRMED and already stated (Sections 4.2 and 5); the roadmap does not list fair tuning as a follow-up

fidelity_scope.verdict: CONFIRMED and already stated as a limit; full CIFAR and LM trajectories with correlated streams are not named as the first follow-up
